articles.title: Parents say police were called because their 3-year-old was 'too good' at soccer. Now Ms. Rachel is involved.
articles.summary: The parents of a 3-year-old soccer phenom who went viral say his youth league called police on them because their son is "too good." But a league official to...
articles.body:
A 3-year-old soccer phenom and his parents in Winter Park, Fla., have gone viral after posting a video in which the family says they were asked to leave the field during a soccer game because the child was playing too well.

In the video taken Saturday, Nevada, the young soccer player, is seen repeatedly scoring goals against children on the opposing team. His parents, Martasia and Don, are heard cheering for him before the video cuts to their conversation with officers from the Winter Park Police Department, who were called to the field.

"They called the police on a 3-year-old because he's too good," Don is heard saying in the clip. "They called the police on a 3-year-old because he had the ball for too long."

However, body-camera video released by Winter Park police showed an official with the youth soccer league, i9 Sports, telling officers that Nevada is a good player but that he pushes too much. He alleged that Nevada's parents "created a big scene, arguing with parents" after he tried to intervene. He also alleged that the parents called him "ignorant" a few weeks earlier for taking their son out of the game to let other kids play.

In a 911 call released by Winter Park police, the i9 Sports official could also be heard saying that while it's "not really an emergency," he wanted to report an "unruly parent" who was being "really disruptive." The official said the parent was following him around the field and calling him names.

After the incident, i9 Sports removed Nevada from the league and issued a refund for his fall registration.

The viral video caught the attention of Rachel Griffin-Accurso, the YouTuber, activist and children's educator better known as Ms. Rachel, who made an Instagram post on Monday calling for "famous soccer players" to show up for Nevada and "shower him with love and awesome experiences."

In the caption of her post, Ms. Rachel condemned the incident as "racist, sick, traumatizing and disgusting," writing, "I'm LIVID! Please sports people give him all the experiences and love. @nevadaney10 We'd love to have him on our show to share his amazing skills. I need sports people to show up for him."

In a statement obtained by News 6 , a local news station in Orlando, i9 Sports said it was "aware of concerns being shared regarding an incident at a local i9 Sports program" and that it's taking them "very seriously."

"The respectful treatment and well-being of every child and family matter deeply to us," the statement read. "We have reached out to the family and have begun a review that includes speaking with those involved. While we work to understand the circumstances, we will not speculate or share unverified information. We appreciate everyone who has brought their concerns to our attention."

The Winter Park Police Department issued its own statement outlining its response to the dispute, including that it was "contacted by a soccer league official" following "a disturbance between league officials and the parents of a player."

"The league requested the family leave and offered to refund the league cost to family. Shortly after arrival, the officers were requested by the league official to communicate with the family as he did not want to further a disturbance. The family stated the game was over and they were leaving," the statement said. "The family was cooperative with the officers. … No one was arrested, trespassed, or forced to leave the park. The Officers body worn cameras confirm the above information."

In an interview with HuffPost , Martasia said the incident "really traumatized" Nevada. While he wants to continue playing soccer, he "doesn't want to go back to that place."

"I don't think that's how he should be thinking, that as a 3-year-old he did something wrong," Martasia said.

Nevada, who had been playing in the league with 5-year-olds, was subjected to unfair treatment on the field, his mother claimed. Martasia said she saw other parents, the league's director and some coaches convene in a circle on the field and suggested that they were trying to figure out how to tell her that Nevada "can't play so other kids could play."

When Martasia approached the group, she said the director told her that "everybody is paying money, so everybody should play." She said the police were called after that, once she started speaking up for Nevada.

"It's heartbreaking because now Nevada's saying he doesn't wanna go over there," Martasia told HuffPost. "He's scared that he did something wrong."

Nevada is set to join a youth soccer training program in January. The program, based in Orlando, is run by Eddie Johnson , a former professional soccer player who heard about what happened in Winter Park.

articles.title: Abstenção cai em todas as 39 cidades da Grande SP; capital concentra cerca de 60% da redução | G1
articles.standfirst: Número de eleitores ausentes caiu em cerca de 465 mil entre os dois turnos; cientista política aponta que eleições apertadas e mobilização podem estimular comparecimento às urnas.
articles.summary: Número de eleitores ausentes caiu em cerca de 465 mil entre os dois turnos; cientista política aponta que eleições apertadas e mobilização podem estimular comparecimento às urnas.
articles.body:
A abstenção caiu nas 39 cidades da região metropolitana de São Paulo no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais , realizado no domingo (25), em comparação com o primeiro turno. Juntos, os municípios tiveram 465.515 ausências a menos, e a capital paulista concentrou cerca de 60% dessa redução.

No primeiro turno, 3.713.715 eleitores deixaram de votar nos 39 municípios. No segundo, foram 3.248.200. Considerando os percentuais agregados, a taxa de abstenção passou de aproximadamente 22,81% para 19,97%, queda de 2,84 pontos percentuais.

Na cidade de São Paulo , o número de eleitores ausentes passou de 2.137.873 no primeiro turno para 1.861.898 no segundo, uma redução de 275.975. Sozinha, a capital respondeu por cerca de 59,3% da queda no número de ausências registrada nas 39 cidades da Grande São Paulo.

A redução no número de ausências, porém, não significa necessariamente que os mesmos eleitores que faltaram no primeiro turno compareceram no segundo. Os números mostram a diferença entre o total de ausentes nas duas votações.

Especialistas ouvidos pela TV Globo apontam que disputas acirradas podem contribuir para mobilizar eleitores entre o primeiro e o segundo turno, como a ocorrida nestas eleições, além da forte presença da militância nas redes sociais e campanhas que levaram jovens às ruas (leia mais abaixo).

No domingo, o presidente reeleito ao inédito quarto mandato, Lula (PT), venceu seu adversário Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em 21 dos 39 municípios da Grande São Paulo. Ele reverteu vantagem em cidades como Osasco e Cotia . Diadema e Francisco Morato registraram os maiores percentuais de Lula (PT), enquanto Guararema e Santa Isabel tiveram as maiores votações proporcionais de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

Entre os 39 municípios, Diadema registrou a maior redução na taxa de abstenção: o índice passou de 22,61% no primeiro turno para 19,02% no segundo, uma queda de 3,59 pontos percentuais.

Na sequência aparecem Carapicuíba, onde a taxa recuou de 25,14% para 21,70%, uma diferença de 3,44 pontos percentuais, e Taboão da Serra, que passou de 19,57% para 16,17%, queda de 3,40 pontos percentuais.

Em Jandira, a abstenção caiu de 21,15% para 17,94%, redução de 3,21 pontos percentuais. Em Embu das Artes, o índice passou de 21,81% para 18,65%, queda de 3,16 pontos percentuais. Francisco Morato teve redução semelhante, também de 3,16 pontos percentuais.

Votação para presidente no 2º turno: dados por local de votação - Diadema (SP) - Veja locais de votação em que Lula venceu e onde Flávio Bolsonaro ficou à frente. - Diadema SP - presidente 2026 turno-2 - quadrado_g1 g1-alt bubble - 26/10/2026 — Foto: Arte G1

Franco da Rocha registrou a menor queda na taxa de abstenção entre as 39 cidades da região. O índice passou de 25,92% no primeiro turno para 25,59% no segundo, recuo de apenas 0,33 ponto percentual.

Mesmo com a redução, o município teve a maior taxa de abstenção da Grande São Paulo no segundo turno. Na outra ponta, São Caetano do Sul registrou o menor índice entre os municípios analisados, com 14,68%.

A cientista política Lara Mesquita analisou os números após o resultado da eleição e apontou que disputas acirradas podem contribuir para mobilizar eleitores entre o primeiro e o segundo turno.

A mobilização nas redes sociais e as campanhas que levaram jovens às ruas também são apontadas na análise como fatores que podem ter incentivado o comparecimento às urnas.

Mesquita chama atenção ainda para os grupos em que o voto é facultativo, como jovens de 16 e 17 anos e pessoas com 70 anos ou mais. Segundo a análise, a abstenção costuma ser maior nesses grupos, mas eleitores dessas faixas também compareceram no segundo turno, depois de terem registrado mais ausências no primeiro.

Os dados mostram que a participação eleitoral aumentou em todas as 39 cidades da Grande São Paulo, embora em proporções diferentes. As variações, por si só, não permitem determinar quanto da queda da abstenção pode ser atribuído a cada iniciativa de mobilização.

Entenda a diferença entre abstenção, voto em branco e voto nulo

As três situações têm significados diferentes. A abstenção corresponde à ausência do eleitor na votação. Já os votos em branco e nulos são registrados por quem comparece às urnas, mas não destina um voto válido a nenhum dos candidatos daquele cargo.

Abstenção: ocorre quando a pessoa apta a votar não comparece à votação.

Voto em branco: é registrado quando o eleitor aperta a tecla “branco” e, depois, “confirma” na urna eletrônica.

Voto nulo: ocorre quando o eleitor digita um número que não corresponde a nenhum candidato ao cargo e confirma.

articles.title: Mais de 3 mil opções mostram que escolher o acabamento certo vai além da estética  | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais do que seguir tendências, definir os materiais da obra passa por entender onde e como cada um será utilizado.
articles.summary: Mais do que seguir tendências, definir os materiais da obra passa por entender onde e como cada um será utilizado.
articles.body:
Entrar em uma loja e encontrar milhares de alternativas pode ser inspirador, mas também traz uma dúvida comum para quem está construindo ou reformando, como identificar o que realmente funciona em cada parte da casa?

Na Vilarejo, são mais de 3 mil opções entre diferentes categorias, formatos, superfícies e acabamentos. Diante desse repertório, o primeiro filtro não precisa ser a cor ou o desenho que mais chamou atenção. Local de aplicação, frequência de uso e condições às quais cada superfície estará exposta ajudam a direcionar a decisão.

Uma sala, por exemplo, apresenta exigências diferentes de um banheiro ou de uma área externa. Resistência, contato com umidade, facilidade de manutenção e características da superfície entram nessa análise e reduzem gradualmente o número de alternativas.

É nesse momento que a variedade deixa de representar apenas quantidade e passa a responder a necessidades distintas dentro de uma mesma obra.

O atendimento especializado ajuda a transformar a variedade em alternativas mais adequadas para cada ambiente, considerando uso, características técnicas e necessidades do projeto — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Antes de olhar para tendências, vale entender as condições do local onde o produto será instalado.

A aplicação indica quais características precisam receber mais atenção. A partir daí, entram formato, acabamento, tonalidade e a relação daquela superfície com os demais elementos da composição.

Em áreas integradas, manter uma linguagem próxima entre os pisos pode contribuir para a continuidade visual. Em outras situações, a mudança de revestimento ajuda a indicar diferentes funções ou destacar uma região específica.

O tamanho das peças também interfere nessa leitura. Grandes formatos valorizam desenhos inspirados em pedras e outras referências naturais com menos interrupções. Peças menores, por sua vez, abrem espaço para paginações, ritmos e detalhes que transformam a própria disposição do revestimento em parte da composição.

Não existe uma fórmula que funcione para todos os casos. São as condições de uso, as características do espaço e o resultado esperado que começam a transformar milhares de alternativas em um conjunto menor e mais coerente.

Fotografias e referências são importantes para identificar preferências, mas nem sempre mostram exatamente como uma superfície será percebida depois de instalada.

Brilho, textura, relevo, veios e variações de tonalidade reagem à iluminação. Por isso, os showrooms da Vilarejo contam com mesas de especificação que permitem observar os materiais sob diferentes temperaturas de luz, comparando como cada acabamento se comporta em condições mais quentes ou mais frias.

Nesse momento, revestimentos, metais e outros elementos podem ser aproximados. Em vez de analisar cada item separadamente, é possível observar as relações entre cores, texturas e superfícies.

Um bege que parece discreto sozinho, por exemplo, pode ganhar outra leitura quando colocado ao lado de madeira, pedra ou metal. Essa comparação antecipa parte do efeito que só seria percebido depois da instalação.

A comparação entre luz fria e luz quente mostra como a iluminação pode alterar a percepção de cores, veios e texturas antes da definição dos acabamentos — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Depois de definir os produtos, surge outra etapa importante: planejar como eles serão distribuídos.

Medidas do local, dimensões das peças, alinhamentos, direção do assentamento e recortes interferem no resultado visual e no aproveitamento do revestimento.

A Vilarejo oferece serviço de paginação, que permite estudar essa distribuição antes da execução. Dessa forma, encontros, posicionamentos e cortes podem ser visualizados ainda durante o planejamento, reduzindo decisões que normalmente só apareceriam no momento da instalação.

Os projetistas internos também participam dessa etapa, relacionando as referências apresentadas pelo cliente às dimensões e necessidades reais do espaço.

Assim, a definição dos acabamentos deixa de acontecer apenas diante da exposição da loja. Comparação, visualização e planejamento passam a fazer parte do caminho até a obra.

Nem todo mundo começa uma reforma sabendo exatamente o que procura. Muitas vezes, o ponto de partida é uma fotografia salva, determinada textura, uma combinação de cores ou simplesmente a vontade de transformar um cômodo.

O Vilarejo de Ideias ajuda a aproximar essas referências de aplicações reais. Os ambientes montados permitem observar produtos em contexto e perceber relações de escala, cor e acabamento que nem sempre ficam evidentes quando uma peça é vista isoladamente.

Tendências podem indicar caminhos, mas precisam fazer sentido para a rotina, para as condições do local e para as expectativas de quem utilizará a casa.

Ambientes montados ajudam a visualizar combinações de revestimentos, metais, cores e texturas em uma escala mais próxima do resultado final — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Ter mais de 3 mil opções amplia os caminhos de uma obra. O desafio está em saber quais critérios utilizar para chegar às alternativas que realmente fazem sentido.

Aplicação, uso, resistência, formato e acabamento ajudam a conduzir essa análise. Comparar superfícies sob diferentes iluminações, estudar a paginação e visualizar combinações acrescenta uma dimensão prática antes da compra.

Nesse contexto, escolher bem não significa analisar o maior número possível de produtos. Significa entender melhor cada necessidade e usar informação, comparação e planejamento para chegar a uma decisão mais adequada para a obra.

articles.title: Pernambucana confronta Eduardo Bolsonaro em seção nos EUA; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Maria Eugênia Carvalho acompanhava manifestação em apoio a Lula (PT) quando encontrou ex-deputado, condenado a 4 anos e 2 meses por coação no processo sobre tentativa de golpe.
articles.summary: Maria Eugênia Carvalho acompanhava manifestação em apoio a Lula (PT) quando encontrou ex-deputado, condenado a 4 anos e 2 meses por coação no processo sobre tentativa de golpe.
articles.body:
A turismóloga pernambucana Maria Eugênia Carvalho, de 61 anos, protagonizou uma discussão com o ex-deputado federal Eduardo Bolsonaro , irmão do senador Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ), candidato derrotado na disputa pela Presidência da República. Os dois discutiram em uma seção eleitoral no Miami Dade College, na Flórida (EUA), durante o 2º turno das eleições, no domingo (25).

Nas imagens, que viralizaram nas redes sociais, Maria Eugênia se aproxima do local onde Eduardo estava, com um grupo de apoiadores, e grita "Eduardo fugitivo" e "volta para o Brasil" (veja vídeo acima) . Eduardo mora nos Estados Unidos desde o início de 2025 e teve o mandato cassado por excesso de faltas . Em junho deste ano, foi condenado a 4 anos e 2 meses de prisão por coação no processo sobre a tentativa de golpe que condenou o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL).

A brasileira acompanhava uma mobilização em apoio ao presidente Lula (PT), que foi reeleito com 64.256.232 votos (51,79% ). Ao g1 , Maria Eugênia contou que já tinha votado quando tudo aconteceu, mas continuava no local para dar apoio a eleitores que não queriam votar sozinhos. Ela mora há oito anos nos EUA com o marido, que é jornalista.

"Eu não dormi do sábado para o domingo com medo. Estava na mobilização incrível com o 'Exército de Lula', comandado por Janones, estava muito instigada, com adrenalina danada, e, quando eu vi aquele cara, na minha frente, de frente para um fugitivo, chamando Lula de ladrão, eu disse: 'ah, não, eu vou lá'", contou.

Maria Eugênia disse que a discussão foi de manhã e afirmou que Eduardo respondeu com deboche. "Ele fez coraçãozinho pra mim. Aquela arrogância", disse.

Pernambucana discute com Eduardo Bolsonaro em seção eleitoral nos Estados Unidos — Foto: Reprodução/WhatsApp

A pernambucana também contou que não teve medo de sofrer uma agressão física por causa do policiamento que estava no local.

"O policiamento é muito grande. Tanto que, no vídeo, você vê o policial olhando, mas eles não podem tocar em mim. Diferente do Brasil, que tem uma agressão física, aqui ninguém pode tocar em você. Então, assim, eu estava muito tranquila", disse.

Durante a discussão, outros eleitores manifestaram apoio à família Bolsonaro e também gritaram para Maria Eugênia "voltar para o Brasil".

Depois, a turismóloga voltou para o grupo de brasileiros que estavam com ela no local. Segundo Maria Eugênia, os organizadores da seção eleitoral orientaram os participantes a deixar a área embaixo do prédio e permanecer no estacionamento, para evitar confusões.

articles.title: Trump faz insinuações e afirma, sem provas, que eleição no Brasil pareceu fraudada; Alckmin rebate | G1
articles.standfirst: Em todo o continente americano, esquerda e direita se uniram e reconheceram a reeleição do presidente Lula.
articles.summary: Em todo o continente americano, esquerda e direita se uniram e reconheceram a reeleição do presidente Lula.
articles.body:
Chefes de governo de países das Américas, tanto de esquerda quanto de direita, enviaram, nesta segunda-feira (26), os parabéns ao presidente Lula . Mas o presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , levantou suspeitas sobre a lisura da votação - sem apresentar provas.

Donald Trump passou o dia em silêncio, sem se manifestar sobre a eleição no Brasil. No fim da tarde, levantou suspeitas sobre a votação, sem apresentar nenhum indício de irregularidade :

“Pareceu terrível para mim, achei que foi terrível. Eu não tomei partido, mas me pareceu mais uma eleição fraudulenta. Francamente, não tomei partido, mas passou uma imagem péssima para o mundo. É mais uma eleição... Sabe, eleições têm que ser incontestáveis, e me pareceu muito ruim. Não tomei partido, não apoiei ninguém nem nada, mas acompanhei a eleição. Pareceu algo tão, mas tão corrupto, algo terrível”.

Questionado sobre o que pretendia fazer, Trump falou da boa relação com Lula:

“Eu não governo o Brasil, eu governo os Estados Unidos. Só achei a eleição... Eu gosto do Lula, me dou muito bem com ele. Só acho que pareceu muito ruim. A eleição, a maneira como foi organizada, a extensão, foi muito estranha”.

Trump faz insinuações e afirma, sem provas, que eleição no Brasil pareceu fraudada; Alckmin rebate — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No Brasil, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin rejeitou a declaração do presidente americano:

“Totalmente equivocada, né? Primeiro não se interfere na política de outro país. Essa é uma regra basilar. Segundo, não tem nenhum referencial para dizer isso. Aliás, o Brasil é um exemplo para o mundo. De urna eletrônica, de segurança jurídica. Democracia é assim. Você ganha eleição, você perde a eleição, é o povo que decide. Mas o caminho é o caminho da negociação”.

Em todo o continente americano, esquerda e direita se uniram e reconheceram a vitória de Lula. Quase todos os presidentes de direita da América do Sul parabenizaram o presidente reeleito e reforçaram a aliança com o Brasil. O presidente do Chile foi um dos primeiros a telefonar para o presidente eleito. José Antonio Kast afirmou:

"Seguiremos trabalhando por uma agenda que potencialize a integração econômica e o combate ao crime organizado na região”.

O presidente da Colômbia , Abelardo de la Espriella, lembrou que Lula apoiou seu adversário na eleição colombiana e que ele apoiou Flávio Bolsonaro, e completou:

“Quando o povo se pronuncia nas urnas, a vontade é respeitada porque é sagrada. Nisso consiste a democracia. Temos diferenças políticas e ideológicas, mas nenhuma consideração pode estar acima dos interesses de nossas nações. O respeito mútuo, a soberania e a cooperação devem marcar nossas relações”.

O presidente do Paraguai , Santiago Peña, disse que os dois países compartilham uma agenda comum de desenvolvimento. Daniel Noboa, do Equador , também defendeu a cooperação:

“Nossa região tem inimigos comuns, desafios compartilhados e muito a ganhar quando trabalhamos juntos”.

Também de direita, os presidentes da Bolívia e do Peru defenderam o fortalecimento das relações. Assim como os presidentes do Uruguai e de Cuba , aliados do presidente Lula.

O argentino, Javier Milei , que protagonizou diversos embates com Lula ao longo da campanha, não se pronunciou.

Na América do Norte, a presidente do México , Cláudia Sheinbaum, apareceu diante das câmeras celebrando:

“É um sopro de ar fresco para a América Latina e para o Caribe”.

E o primeiro-ministro do Canadá , Mark Carney, escreveu:

“Vamos criar grandes oportunidades de comércio, proteger o meio ambiente e construir prosperidade para nossos povos”.

articles.title: Mega-Sena pode pagar R$ 305 milhões nesta terça-feira; g1 transmite | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.076 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 305 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta terça-feira (27), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última segunda (26), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Mesmo derrotado, Flávio Bolsonaro venceu com folga em alguns países | G1
articles.standfirst: Apesar da vitória de Lula na disputa presidencial, os resultados da votação entre brasileiros que vivem fora do país revelaram cenários bastante diferentes em alguns locais.
articles.summary: Apesar da vitória de Lula na disputa presidencial, os resultados da votação entre brasileiros que vivem fora do país revelaram cenários bastante diferentes em alguns locais.
articles.body:
O candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, falou após ser derrotado na eleição, no dia 26 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Agustin Marcarian/Reuters

Neste domingo (25), brasileiros espalhados pelo mundo foram às urnas para decidir quem ocupará o Palácio do Planalto pelos próximos quatro anos. O resultado foi uma vitória apertada de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) , com 51,79% dos votos, contra 48,21% de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) . Apesar da disputa acirrada, houveram alguns países onde o candidato do PL liderou com folga.

Um deles foi o Nepal , no sul da Ásia. Por lá, dos 32 brasileiros aptos a votar, Flávio recebeu 12 votos, contra apenas um de Lula — o equivalente a 92,31% e 7,69% dos votos válidos, respectivamente.

No primeiro turno, o candidato do PL também havia conquistado uma vitória expressiva no país, com 84,62% dos votos.

Já na América do Sul, o Paraguai também registrou uma ampla vantagem para Flávio Bolsonaro. Em Salto del Guairá, cidade localizada na fronteira com Mato Grosso do Sul, o senador recebeu 576 votos (95,84%), contra apenas 25 (4,16%) de Lula .

Já, em Ciudad del Este, na fronteira com Foz do Iguaçu (PR), o cenário foi semelhante: Flávio conquistou 91,52% dos votos, contra 4,16% do petista.

Ao todo, Flávio Bolsonaro recebeu 4.542 votos no Paraguai, contra 703 de Lula — o equivalente a 86,60% e 13,40% dos votos válidos, respectivamente.

Veja como foi as eleição presidencial no exterior — Foto: Bruna Azevedo/Arte g1

Ao todo, 90 países registraram votos no 2º turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras e Lula o mais votado em 62, enquanto Flávio liderou em 38. Na comparação com o primeiro turno, o candidato do PL virou o resultado em três países e três cidades, enquanto o petista passou à frente em dois países e sete cidades.

A votação no exterior foi organizada em 186 cidades de 134 países e territórios, incluindo a Guiana Francesa.

Mais de 916 mil brasileiros estavam aptos a votar no exterior, mas apenas 381.443 compareceram às urnas.

Segundo o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), a abstenção foi de 58,37%. Apesar do índice, cerca de 40 mil eleitores a mais votaram no segundo turno em comparação com o primeiro.

Ao todo, 9.762 eleitores votaram nulo ou em branco.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) : 171.497 (46,14%)

Na comparação com o segundo turno de 2022, Lula recebeu 47.249 votos a mais no exterior. Na disputa contra Jair Bolsonaro (PL), o petista havia obtido 152.905 votos (51,28%), contra 145.264 (48,72%) do então presidente.

articles.title: Fotógrafo registra 'mar de nuvens' na Serra Gaúcha e vídeo viraliza | G1
articles.standfirst: Rafael Santos acampou no Pico Monte Claro, em Veranópolis, e usou técnica de timelapse durante 3h30 para gravar o amanhecer. Fenômeno é causado por resfriamento e alta umidade.
articles.summary: Rafael Santos acampou no Pico Monte Claro, em Veranópolis, e usou técnica de timelapse durante 3h30 para gravar o amanhecer. Fenômeno é causado por resfriamento e alta umidade
articles.body:
Um fotógrafo captou o nascer do sol em meio a um "mar de nuvens" a 715 metros acima do nível do mar . A imagem viralizou nas redes sociais e já ultrapassou 1,7 milhão de visualizações. O registro foi feito por Rafael Santos no Pico Monte Claro, em Veranópolis , na Serra Gaúcha, na madrugada da quarta-feira (21). Veja o vídeo acima.

☁️ Segundo a Climatempo Meteorologia, o fenômeno do vídeo é um nevoeiro causado pelo resfriamento noturno e pela umidade alta.

"A transição das estrelas pro amanhecer, junto com o movimento do mar de nuvens. É uma forma de enxergar a natureza de um jeito que normalmente nossos olhos não conseguem perceber."

O fotógrafo mora em Novo Hamburgo , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre , e percorreu cerca de 130 quilômetros até o local, onde foi acampar com a noiva e aproveitou para fazer as imagens. "Essa época do ano é propícia pra ver o fenômeno", afirma.

Por volta das 2h, ele começou a fotografar as estrelas, mas relata que as condições de tempo não estavam propícias . Então decidiu montar o equipamento para gravar o amanhecer .

"Usei uma técnica chamada timelapse, em que a câmera faz centenas de fotos em intervalos programados. Depois, junto todas elas em sequência, criando esse efeito de passagem acelerada do tempo", explica.

Santos conta que fez alguns testes, conectou a câmera em uma tomada do camping e foi para outro ponto. Por volta das 5h20, ele foi conferir se tinha dado certo e para ver ao vivo ao nascer do sol. No total, foram 3h30 de captação de imagens para montar o vídeo .

Ele diz que, apesar de trabalhar com fotografia e produção audiovisual na área corporativa e publicitária, a fotografia de natureza é uma paixão .

"Na Islândia, tive a oportunidade de fotografar a aurora boreal, no deserto do Atacama, no Chile, fotografei o céu noturno e também já fiz registros na Patagônia argentina. Mas cada lugar é diferente, principalmente porque a gente depende muito das condições da natureza", comenta.

O fotógrafo diz que ficou muito feliz com o resultado e mais ainda quando viu a repercussão do vídeo .

"Queria compartilhar um pouco das paisagens incríveis que temos aqui no Rio Grande do Sul. Ver tanta gente comentando, compartilhando e se encantando com o vídeo é muito gratificante", conclui

articles.title: María Machado returns from exile to a Venezuela reshaped by Trump
articles.summary: Machado returns with Trump's blessing, even if Washington is happy with Venezuela's existing leader - at least for the time being.
articles.body:
Driving down roads lined with jubilant supporters from the western state of Lara to the capital Caracas, Maria Corina Machado's return to Venezuela could hardly have been more different to her exit 10 months earlier.

Colourful, loud, open and defiant, it stood in stark contrast to the way the Venezuelan opposition leader slipped out of the country in the dead of night in December last year to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo.

She had been unable to make it back to her homeland until now, thwarted on several occasions by the Venezuelan government - and by the Trump administration, which insisted the "time wasn't right" for her return.

"Maria Corina is the indisputable leader of Venezuela," says 20-year-old Gregory Noriega, wearing a sweatshirt emblazoned with the logo of the opposition movement Vente Venezuela. "Her return represents hope."

"This is a step forward in the electoral process which we've been waiting for since last year," echoes 18-year-old Hilary, who turned out on to the streets of the capital hoping to catch a glimpse of the opposition leader on her victory lap.

"She's returned after the double earthquakes when Venezuela needs her," adds her friend, Manuel. "The whole country is behind her to show that now Venezuela isn't scared."

Much has changed since Machado left Venezuelan soil to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

Then-President Nicolás Maduro is no longer at the top of the Venezuelan government.

Maduro was forcibly removed from power by US troops on 3 January, and whisked to New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges – to which he's pleaded not guilty.

He was replaced by his former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez, who has turned the page with Washington in ways few could have imagined.

The bilateral relationship is today unrecognisable from the years of mutual animosity during the reigns of President Hugo Chávez and then his handpicked successor, Maduro.

The new circumstances throw up some interesting conundrums for both sides.

When Machado left Venezuela, she had long been considered Washington's favoured alternative to Maduro. She returns to find the Trump administration perfectly happy with the one they've got – at least for the time being.

The Trump administration recently signed a major oil deal with Venezuela which gave the US a 100-year concession over a staggering 65bn barrels of Venezuelan crude oil.

The deal was reached in conjunction with a Venezuelan private company called North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) run by a businessman with a chequered past, Alejandro Betancourt.

Machado has openly criticised the deal which the Rodríguez government reached with the US, albeit careful to direct her criticism at Caracas and at Betancourt rather than President Trump, to whom she gave her peace prize and whose trust and support she craves to move forward.

President Trump has repeatedly said how satisfied he is with Delcy Rodríguez, calling her "wonderful" and "a terrific person". This was the vice-president of an administration he previously described as made up of "narco-communists".

But the outpouring of jubilation for Machado's caravan into the capital shows she can still count on significant support on the streets, says Venezuelan political analyst Beningno Alarcon.

"The return of Maria Corina Machado, in my personal view, is the most significant [political] event since 3rd January," says Alarcon. "It means the most important political leader in Venezuela is back in the country."

"The reception for her return shows that her ability to mobilise her support remains intact, which means the opposition in Venezuela now has something very solid: a leadership which is present on the ground as opposed to solely in exile," he says.

Alarcon provides some evidence that the opposition – and the public at large – feel more emboldened since 3 January, a situation he believes will become only more pronounced with Machado's reappearance.

For instance, a joint study by the political think tanks Polis and Nexo suggests that Venezuela saw three times as many street protests in the first nine months of this year as in all of 2025, with demonstrations spanning a range of issues, from politics and working conditions to water supply.

Furthermore, there's evidence that the repression of such protests has reduced by more than half.

In such an environment, the return of a figurehead like Machado can galvanise an electorate that has spent years fearful of the consequences of speaking out.

Her return also needs to be seen within the context of the wider talks brokered by Washington between the Venezuelan government and the opposition towards a negotiated political solution.

Certainly, the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, was quick to say her "safe return" to Venezuela was "the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks".

The Nobel Peace Prize winner still faces charges in Venezuela ranging from treason to conspiracy of insurrection. For years, she and her supporters have dismissed the charges as politically motivated and baseless.

Having made at least eight attempts to return to Venezuela by air and by sea before the Trump administration gave her the green light, Machado now knows she has Trump's blessing to be back on home soil – a position Delcy Rodríguez is both unwilling and unlikely to challenge.

She called Machado's return a "show" and the entire cross-country event, which was livestreamed by her supporters over the weekend, was studiously ignored by state television outlets.

But Rodríguez, too, needs a harmonious relationship with Washington if she is to avoid a fate similar to that of her predecessor and indicated she might be prepared to hold talks with Machado.

For as much as Trump has complimented Rodríguez, he has also made it clear that Washington expects nothing less than her full submission and malleability on key issues like energy.

Some reports have even suggested all major decision-making in the oil-rich nation is being largely dictated by Secretary Rubio via regular WhatsApp calls to the interim president.

The young supporters gathered in droves in Caracas to cheer Maria Corina Machado home say their fears of criticising their government or demanding change are vanishing.

Her return marked an irreversible political transition in Venezuela, they insist, one which they could barely fathom when she left for Oslo just a year ago.

Additional reporting by Vanessa Silva in Caracas.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'England's golden boy' and 'Time to pay fair'
articles.summary: Many of the papers consider what will be in the Budget and praise Harry Kane for his Ballon d'Or win.
articles.body:
Several of the papers lead on measures that are expected to be in the Budget.

The Guardian says Chancellor John Healey will scrap what's seen as the cliff-edge rule for unpaid carers . Currently they have to forfeit their entire week's carers' allowance - of more than £86 - if they earn just one penny above £204 in that week. The paper says that under the new rules, only £1 will be removed from the allowance for every £1 above the earning limit.

On its front page the Times says Healey will announce plans to increase the minimum wage by nearly 4% for workers aged 21 and over, but not for those aged 18 to 21. The paper says that, in effect, spells the end for Labour's manifesto pledge to bring the minimum wage for younger people in line with that for older workers.

The Daily Mirror highlights a call by trade unions for higher taxes on banks . The paper says bosses running Britain's big four banks take just two days to earn what a typical worker makes in a whole year. But the Daily Mail says raising taxes on banks would be "a folly in the extreme," because "for all their faults" the banks drive the economy, and if you tax them more heavily you punish every corporation and every small and medium-sized enterprise in the country.

Charities providing end-of-life care have told the Daily Express that Healey should announce a £200m annual injection for their sector. The paper says almost six-in-10 hospices in England have either made or are considering cuts to frontline services.

According to the i Paper, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmoud is furious at Andy Burnham because members of the cabinet were not warned before he called for a debate about a return to freedom of movement with the EU. A government source told the paper the Prime Minister's comments had undermined Mahmood's strategy to reduce immigration. The Sun says restoring freedom of movement would be a catastrophe for getting the jobless back into work, for wages, public services and social cohesion.

And the Daily Telegraph reports that guidance has been issued for teachers to help them uncover essays written by artificial intelligence. The document lists dozens of words, phrases and stylistic features - such as "delve," "catalyst," and "in conclusion" - which, it says, could indicate use of AI tools, if they appear frequently.

The paper reports that the national living wage, which applies to those 21 and over, and the national minimum wage, which applies to those aged 18 to 21, will both increase by 3.9%. "England's golden boy" Harry Kane also features on the front page, pictured holding the men's Ballon d'Or award.

articles.title: Ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump goes into effect in Russian-occupied town ‘on the brink of disaster’
articles.summary: The agreement would “temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation,” the White House said.
articles.body: A rare humanitarian ceasefire brokered by first lady Melania Trump to save people trapped in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian town went into effect early Tuesday. After months of warnings from Ukrainian officials about an unraveling humanitarian catastrophe in the front-line town of Oleshky, in the southern Kherson region, the White House announced last week that the first lady had secured a pause in the fighting. The agreement between Ukraine and Russia would “temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” according to a statement released Friday. Both the Ukrainian and Russian militaries have confirmed that the ceasefire will start at 3 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET) to ensure what they have both called a “humanitarian operation.” Neither side has indicated when the temporary truce would end. The ceasefire announcement came amid renewed pressure from President Donald Trump on his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which began when Russia ⁠invaded Ukraine in February 2022. In recent weeks, Ukraine has complained of gaps in intelligence sharing from the U.S. and a slowdown of Elon Musk’s Starlink service, which is crucial for its military. Earlier this month, Trump also eased some sanctions on the Kremlin allowing Russia to supply diesel to the global market in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the midterm elections, reversing years of American policy — a move that raised alarm in Ukraine and Europe. But in a rare intervention from the first lady, the White House statement quoted her as saying that Oleshky was “on the brink of disaster” and its remaining population, composed primarily of elderly residents, was in urgent need of medical attention, medicine, food and clean water. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks,” she said. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” Civilian representatives from both sides will visit the town, which had a population of around 24,000 people before the war, to determine the level of assistance the remaining residents require, the statement said. An “impartial American media organization” will document the process to ensure “that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected,” it added. The ceasefire is likely to last several days as the Russian side has to “clear the roads of mines,” Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukraine’s TSN TV channel Sunday, adding that his forces would have to verify the area is clear. “There is no doubt that Russia will do everything it can to clear the roads of mines so that these people head toward Russia and stay there. They are not going to simply let people go,” he said. Both sides blame each other for the crisis in Oleshky. Kyiv has accused Russian forces of mining nearby roads and using the remaining residents as human shields to prevent Ukraine’s army from conducting offensive operations in the town. Meanwhile, Russia has blamed Ukraine for “laying siege to the town” with drone strikes and preventing humanitarian aid from getting in. Last month, the Kremlin acknowledged problems with food and medical ​supplies getting into Oleshky, saying its military was working to resolve them. Ukrainian media has for months been featuring interviews with people who have managed to escape Oleshky and spoken to relatives of those who remain there — an estimated 2,000 people, including children. Some said the town was on the verge of starvation and residents were relying on homegrown produce to survive. Others had reportedly resorted to eating grass. With winter looming, fears of famine are growing in the town where communication is difficult because of a severely compromised internet and cellphone service in the area. The United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, which has been documenting the crisis for months, said there have been no food deliveries to the town since the end of May. Oleshky, like a large portion of the Kherson region, has been occupied by Russian forces since the early weeks of the invasion. Drone footage of the town, shared by Ukraine’s 34th Separate Marine Brigade “Borysfen” last month and verified by NBC News, shows the charred ruins of desolate residential and administrative buildings inside the town, in a rare look at the level of destruction. Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, shared another video earlier this month, geolocated by NBC News, showing residents leaving Oleshky on foot, bicycles and mopeds in what he said was a desperate search for food. He said they faced the impossible choice of being blown up on a mine or dying from hunger. Their plight received international attention in recent weeks after Pope Leo XIV directly raised the growing crisis with Putin, and European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno went on a hunger strike, saying “the people of Oleshky cannot be abandoned.” While both Kyiv and Moscow have unilaterally announced Easter or Christmas ceasefires before, they did not revolve around a humanitarian crisis and have not involved open mediation by the U.S., making the Oleshky ceasefire an unprecedented halting of fire between the two sides. The ceasefire could serve as a model for similar humanitarian arrangements in other areas, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday, especially given the “highly positive” American involvement, including the first lady. Melania Trump has been involved in the humanitarian campaign to bring back Ukrainian children taken by Russia, and the White House statement said she leveraged the “communication channel” established through those efforts to bring about a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky.

articles.title: Jordan says 'terrorists' killed in Syria in retaliatory strike over church attack
articles.summary: The attack on a village in Syria killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.
articles.body:
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.

Syrian health officials told state media five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government. Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.

It comes after a nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.

In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan.

"The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, to ensure the safety of travellers and workers at the crossing," Syrian authorities said in a statement carried by state media.

It added that it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and had launched "comprehensive investigations to establish the full circumstances of the targeting".

Nassib is the only passenger and commercial border crossing between Jordan and Syria.

Earlier on Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law over the church attack.

The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed "terrorists" were found hiding in an abandoned house in Karak before dawn.

Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told state-affiliated TV the attackers were all Jordanians and "had been holed up in a building in one of the villages near the site of the attack".

articles.title: New Zealand election 2026: What you need to know
articles.summary: Voters will elect a new parliament on 7 November with the cost of living among the key issues.
articles.body:
New Zealanders will head to the polls on 7 November to elect a new government.

The rising cost of living, unemployment and healthcare are among the main concerns of voters, who will choose members of parliament.

There is no clear frontrunner, based on pre-election polls. The incumbent centre-right prime minister, Christopher Luxon, won the last election in 2023 with a promise to "build the economy".

Here is everything you need to know about New Zealand's 2026 general election.

New Zealand holds a general election every three years and uses a Mixed-Member Proportional system or MMP.

Each voter makes two choices - the representative of their constituency in parliament and a political party.

The candidate in a constituency with the most votes wins and becomes an MP.

Political parties on the other hand must win at least 5% of the total party votes to secure a seat in parliament. The seats are also allocated proportionately - if a party wins 40% of the total party votes, it will get 40% of the seats alloted for parties.

The New Zealand parliament typically has 120 seats - 71 are allocated to constituencies and the remaining 49 are distributed to parties proportionately.

New Zealand elections rarely result in an outright majority and parties forge coalitions to form a government.

New Zealand adopted the MMP in 1996 to address concerns that small parties were being left out of the vote.

The current government is led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, whose centre-right National party came to power in 2023 . It governs in coalition with the ACT and New Zealand First parties.

His party emphasised economic management, restoring a budget surplus, and expanding KiwiSaver, New Zealand's retirement savings scheme.

The main opposition is the centre-left Labour party, led by former prime minister Chris Hipkins.

Labour has focused on reducing living costs, improving healthcare and transport, and investing in housing, jobs and public services.

National's coalition partners also have their own priorities. ACT, led by David Seymour, has advocated stricter immigration policies, while New Zealand First, led by Winston Peters, has proposed changes to voting eligibility, with the party proposing that voting in New Zealand should be restricted to citizens only.

The Green Party, co-led by Chlöe Swarbrick and Marama Davidson, is another player. It has campaigned on issues including wealth taxes, renewable energy and public services.

Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, is also competing for parliamentary seats, with housing, healthcare, education and constitutional reform among its priorities.

Cost of living is a major concern for New Zealanders.

A September 2026 Ipsos survey found that 63% of respondents identified inflation and the cost of living as one of the country's most important issues. Healthcare and hospitals came second at 44%, followed by the economy at 34%.

Unemployment is also a growing concern, with 21% of respondents identifying it as a major issue in the same survey. It overtook housing to become New Zealand's fourth most important issue.

Polling places open from 09:00 local time on 7 November (20:00 GMT 6 November). Voting ends at 19:00. Advance voting started on 26 October while overseas voting began earlier on 21 October.

Preliminary results will be released progressively from 19:00 on election night through New Zealand's official election results website. These initial results will not be the official final count.

The Electoral Commission is scheduled to declare official results on 27 November, after the counting and verification process has been completed.

A clear result on election night could provide an early indication of which parties are best placed to form a government. However, a tight race could delay negotiations if no party wins an outright majority.

New Zealanders may therefore have to wait beyond election night to find out which parties will form the next government and who will lead the country for the next three years.

articles.title: In 2020, a California homeowner applied to build a second dwelling on his property but says the city delayed approval for over three years, causing more than $1 million in losses; an October 23 court revived his lawsuit
articles.summary: A California appeals court has allowed a homeowner's lawsuit against the City of Palos Verdes Estates to move forward after officials allegedly took more
articles.body: A California appeals court has allowed a homeowner's lawsuit against the City of Palos Verdes Estates to move forward after officials allegedly took more than three years to approve his secondary home, causing over $1 million in financial losses. In a ruling published on October 23, the California Court of Appeal, Second Appellate District, Division Four, overturned a lower court decision that had dismissed the case. The three-judge panel found that state laws requiring quick approval of accessory dwelling units, often called granny flats or ADUs, were designed to protect property owners from costly delays caused by local officials. According to court documents published by Justia Law, homeowner Wei Shi first applied to the City of Palos Verdes Estates in 2020 for a permit to build an accessory dwelling unit on his residential property. He planned to build the second home at the same time as the main house on the lot. However, the lawsuit alleges that city officials failed to meet legal deadlines and required reviews that were not allowed under state law. These actions delayed final permit approval until 2023.Allegations of unauthorized reviews and administrative delaysCalifornia law, under Government Code section 66317, requires local governments to review and approve eligible accessory dwelling unit applications through a standard process. This means officials must make a decision without public hearings or discretionary reviews. The law requires local permitting agencies to approve or reject a completed application within 60 days. Despite these clear legal requirements, Shi claimed that the City of Palos Verdes Estates put his application through a lengthy planning process that violated state law. According to the complaint described in the appeals court documents, city staff told Shi that his proposed accessory dwelling unit needed a conditional use permit, discretionary architectural reviews, and formal approval from the Palos Verdes Homes Association Art Jury. The complaint also alleged that a city planning commissioner actively encouraged nearby residents to oppose the project. Because it took three years to receive the building permits, Shi said he suffered major financial losses. The complaint lists several types of damages, including being unable to use the property, rising construction costs, design and professional fees, extra interest payments, and a drop in the property's overall value. The total losses were estimated to exceed $1 million.Trial court dismissal overturned on appealShi first sued the city in October 2024 in the Los Angeles County Superior Court. He sought financial compensation under Government Code section 815.6, part of the California Government Claims Act. This law allows public agencies to be held responsible when they fail to carry out a legal duty that was created to protect people from a specific type of harm. The City of Palos Verdes Estates asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit. City lawyers argued that California's accessory dwelling unit laws were created to address the state's housing shortage for the general public, not to protect individual property owners from financial losses caused by permit delays. The trial court agreed with the city and dismissed the case. It ruled that the permitting laws were intended to increase the state's housing supply, rather than protect individual property owners' financial investments. Shi then appealed the decision.Appeals panel rules mandatory duty protects applicantsIn its decision, the appeals court rejected the city's arguments. The panel found that the legal requirement to approve or reject eligible applications within 60 days was created in part to protect individual applicants from bureaucratic delays. The appeals court explained that increasing housing across California was a major goal of the law. However, the specific requirement for local governments to process permits quickly, without unnecessary discretionary reviews, also protects applicants from extra property expenses and rising construction costs. The court found that Shi had presented a valid legal claim under the Government Claims Act. It therefore overturned the lower court's decision and sent the case back for further proceedings. The ruling allows Shi's lawsuit seeking more than $1 million in damages from the City of Palos Verdes Estates to continue toward trial.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Rise in sales of radios and tinned foods, say retailers, after call to stock up
articles.summary: Figures obtained by BBC Newsnight show large spikes in sales of torches, radios and power banks.
articles.body:
Some retailers have seen a dramatic increase in sales of essential goods after the government called for people to stock up in case of a crisis, according to figures obtained by Newsnight.

The Iceland supermarket chain said it was "clear" consumers had listened to warnings after it saw a 40% increase in sales of tinned products over the weekend.

The rise in sales came after Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said that people should stockpile goods to prepare for an emergency such as a cyber attack or an extreme weather event.

Robert Dyas reported a 160% increase in sales of radios compared with last week, while Maplin said sales had increased by 92% in radios, 284% in torches and 106% in power banks.

The Maplin figures cover the period since the government's announcement last week compared with the same period last month.

"Within hours of the Be Ready announcement we saw people reach for the basics - a torch, a wind-up radio, a power bank. Torch sales nearly quadrupled and radio sales almost doubled in three days," said Ollie Marshall, managing director at Maplin.

"These are simple, affordable products that keep a household connected and informed when the power goes out, and it's encouraging to see people taking the advice seriously."

On 22 October, Streeting said that people should ensure they have three litres of water per person per day; tinned goods in the cupboard; baby food; battery powered torches and mobile phone charging packs.

Many of the items cited by Streeting appeared in the list of goods gathered by Newsnight whose sales have shot up.

In response to the increase in retail sales of certain items, the defence secretary told Newsnight: "It's encouraging that people are taking practical steps to be ready. Having a few everyday essentials at home, from tinned food to torches, helps households prepare for disruption, whether that's flooding, power cuts or burst pipes. We can all play our part in making Britain more resilient."

An Iceland spokesperson told the BBC programme: "It's clear consumers have listened to the government's message as we have seen a 40% increase in sales of tinned products over the weekend and strong sales of bottled water too. Our supplies of these products remain healthy."

Newsnight also spoke to independent retailers who reported a spike in sales of goods highlighted by the defence secretary.

Josh Pringle, from Sgt Prepper's online store, said his sales had increased tenfold: "We were a small outfit on Wednesday. And then the government launched the Be Ready campaign and we couldn't believe what we were seeing – order after order after order. Most of them were for a wind-up radio."

Lincoln Miles, founder of Preppers Shop UK, told Newsnight of a 650% increase in sales after the government announcement. "Everything about off grid seems to be the key of what people are buying for the minute."

articles.title: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
articles.summary: The Duchess of Sussex says she "can't wait" to take part in the programme, which will air next year.
articles.body:
The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-host of the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia.

Meghan will join the 2027 series as a "special guest" with fellow host Poh Ling Yeow, according to Australia's Channel 10.

The duchess said she "can't wait" to take part in the programme after an appearance as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year. It was the show's largest Sunday audience since 2023, according to the statement from Paramount ANZ.

The announcement comes as Meghan faces increased scrutiny due to her father Thomas Markle being accused of child sexual abuse. He denies the allegations.

The BBC understands Meghan broke contact with her father last year , telling him she and authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Markle has strongly rejected the accusations as "lies" which are being used to destroy his reputation.

Will the public change its mind about Meghan?

Meghan's return to Australia follows a four-day tour of the country she and Prince Harry undertook in April.

Meghan's MasterChef debut was announced on the second day of the tour, a Wednesday on which the duchess had been notably absent from public-facing appearances. That evening, it was revealed she had been filming an episode of the programme.

It is understood she was not paid for her appearance. Australia's Network 10, which airs the series as part of Paramount ANZ, did not respond to a question from the BBC about whether Meghan would be paid for co-hosting the Junior MasterChef season.

"I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun," Meghan said in a statement.

In August, the Sussexes announced they were moving back to the UK from California. The couple left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

They embarked on media careers which included a high-profile interview with Oprah Winfrey and a deal with Netflix and Spotify.

Meghan's lifestyle and cookery show on Netflix, With Love, Meghan, ran for two series and a Christmas special but did not perform well with audiences.

She also launched lifestyle brand As Ever, which includes a food range, but in March it ended its partnership with the streaming platform .

Last year her trademark was registered in more than a dozen product categories in Australia, including cookware and table linen.

articles.title: Can a court allow new evidence after a divorce case reaches final arguments? J&K&L high court answers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When a divorce petition reaches court, can one spouse bring up new evidence after both sides have finished presenting their cases?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When a divorce petition reaches court, can one spouse bring up new evidence after both sides have finished presenting their cases? The Jammu and Kashmir high court has explained when a court can allow this, in a divorce case in which a wife recently claimed that her husband had married another woman while they were still married.The high court allowed the wife to present two new witnesses and question her husband again, saying the alleged second marriage could be relevant to the divorce case.Why did the wife seek to present fresh evidence?As per the court order, the husband had filed a divorce petition, accusing his wife of cruelty and desertion, or leaving him without a valid reason. He also alleged that she had not followed a court order requiring her to resume living with him.Both sides presented their evidence in the family court. After the evidence was completed and the case was listed for final arguments, the wife filed an application seeking permission to question her husband again and examine two additional witnesses.She told the family court that she had recently learnt that her husband had allegedly married another woman while his marriage with her was still valid. She claimed that he had three children from that marriage and that she learnt about it after meeting a man who was married to the alleged second wife's daughter.The wife argued that this information was important to her defence in this divorce case.If proved, the alleged second marriage could help explain why she had not returned to live with her husband and could also be relevant to his allegations of cruelty.The husband opposed the application. He argued that the wife already knew about the alleged second marriage and that there was no need to reopen the evidence. He also challenged the family court's decision to impose Rs 10,000 in costs on him for allegedly hiding the marriage.The husband pointed out that the wife had filed a complaint alleging bigamy against him in 1997. That complaint, however, concerned an alleged marriage with a different woman and was dismissed in 2014.When can a court allow new evidence after a trial?Justice Sanjay Dhar examined the rules governing the recall of witnesses and the reopening of evidence. The court explained that judges can recall a witness to clear up doubts about evidence already presented, but this power cannot be routinely used to give either side another chance to fill gaps in its case.The court also noted that judges can use their powers under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to allow fresh evidence in suitable cases when it is relevant and necessary for a fair decision.“If, after the trial of the case, it is established that, in fact, the petitioner, Mangat Ram, had entered into wedlock during the subsistence of his marriage with the respondent, it would have a bearing upon the outcome of the issue as to whether the respondent was justified in not joining the company of the petitioner,” the court said.The court said the alleged second marriage, if established, could also provide a defence against the husband's allegations of cruelty. It found that the documents submitted by the wife appeared to support her claim that the additional evidence could be relevant.“Since important and relevant evidence is sought to be produced by the respondent, it would be necessary for the Court to recall the petitioner, Mangat Ram, to elicit the requisite information and to clarify the doubts arising from the evidence led by the parties on this aspect of the matter,” the court added.However, the court did not agree that all the witnesses should be recalled. It noted that two of the husband's witnesses had already stated during cross-examination that they knew nothing about the alleged second marriage. Recalling them would therefore serve no useful purpose.The family court had directed the husband to pay Rs 10,000 in costs for allegedly concealing his second marriage. The high court said this was premature because the alleged marriage had not yet been proved.“Without recording such a finding, it cannot be stated that the petitioner has concealed the fact with regard to his second marriage. The direction of the learned trial court to this extent is not sustainable in law,” it further added.The high court partly allowed the husband's petition. It upheld the family court's decision to question him again and allow the wife to examine the two new witnesses. The family court was directed to continue hearing the divorce case in line with the high court's observations.

articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen says it has intercepted three ballistic missiles and four drones launched by the Houthis towards Saudi Arabia.

Major-General Turki al-Maliki, the coalition spokesman, said on Tuesday that the missiles were aimed at the kingdom’s Eastern Province and caused no casualties. He added that the drones were headed towards the kingdom’s southern regions.

There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.

Before the interceptions, Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence agency issued emergency alerts in the Eastern Province and the Al Kharj governorate. After lifting them, the agency urged residents to avoid crowds, refrain from filming and call 911 in an emergency.

The coalition had reported the interception and destruction of three additional drones across the Riyadh and southern region on Monday evening.

The attacks came as senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan met their Iranian counterparts in Tehran in an effort to calm a regional conflict that began when the United States and Israel launched a war on Iran in February. The war has reignited the conflict in Yemen.

Saudi Arabia said the visit was meant to open negotiating channels to “prevent the return of military escalation”. The kingdom sent its defence minister, Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, a younger brother of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Pakistan sent its army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkiye sent its intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin.

Iranian state media published pictures of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, attending the meetings.

In a joint statement issued late on Monday, the four countries “agreed to continue the dialogue to strengthen cooperation amongst the four regional countries, including for peace and security in the region”, according to Iranian state media.

Pakistan and Qatar have led the mediation efforts between the US and Iran, which produced an interim peace agreement in June.

Fighting between Iran and the US soon resumed, however, and conflict flared between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia, opening a new front and deepening the humanitarian crisis in Yemen.

The Houthis seized strategic areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed government forces in a lightning offensive last month, prompting a counteroffensive. Saudi Arabia has since intensified its strikes on the group.

The Houthis have also struck Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities. An attack on King Khalid International airport in Riyadh this month killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade.

Earlier on Monday, the Houthis claimed another attack on the Riyadh airport, as well as on crude oil pumping stations in Saudi Arabia’s west and east. The Saudi-led coalition said the missiles were intercepted and destroyed.

It also said it launched retaliatory attacks, destroying five tunnels used by the Houthis to store ballistic missiles, four missile launchers and a missile depot.

The wider war has also restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and driven up oil and petrol prices.

Egypt, a major financial and political partner of Saudi Arabia, has also moved closer to the fight. On Monday, Egypt’s Parliament authorised the military to help defend the kingdom.

articles.title: In 2020, Desiree Heveroh became sole caretaker of a tiny California lighthouse island; when power failed for two months, she relied on a 1930s generator
articles.summary: Discover how Desiree Heveroh navigated a challenging two-month power outage as the sole caretaker of East Brother Light Station, a historic lighthouse island in California, relying on a 1930s generator.
articles.body: Several small, rocky islands in the northern part of San Francisco Bay carry lighthouses that were built in the nineteenth century to guide ships through narrow, fog-prone channels. The keeper’s house stood beside a wooden tower; supplies arrived by ship and whoever lived there operated the light each day. The automation of the twentieth century put an end to resident keepers at many stations, while those buildings that still existed were either left to decay or given over to preservation societies. Operating the station in modern times is quite a different experience. Power can be brought to the island via an underwater cable, the navigation light is often maintained by the Coast Guard and the non-profit organization handles maintenance costs by hosting guests for the night. If anything in that chain fails, the person living on the island is usually the first to notice and has few alternatives.East Brother Light Station, first lit on March 1The US Lighthouse Society’s page for podcast episode 94 gives the station’s background. The page states that Congress appropriated funds in March 1871 for a light on East Brother Island, which lies about 1000 feet offshore on the east side of California’s San Pablo Strait. The Stick Style structure is a wooden square tower built onto a six-bedroom keeper’s residence and the station’s fourth-order lens was first lit on March 1, 1874. The station was automated and unmanned in the summer of 1969. Restoration work on the lighthouse has been carried out by the non-profit East Brother Light Station, Inc., under Coast Guard license and by 1980 it had become available for overnight stays.Desiree Heveroh became resident keeper after the June 2020 closureThe Light Hearted emergency episode from May 2021 explains that the COVID-19 pandemic forced the bed and breakfast to close at the end of June 2020. The resident caretakers left and board member Desiree Heveroh moved in as resident keeper. A KTVU report describes her as a trained volunteer who served as a keeper alongside professional keeper Captain Jarrod Ward and says Ward was sent elsewhere when the light station lost power, leaving her on the island alone. Reports differ slightly on how long she stayed, with Latitude 38 giving 13 months as of August 2021 and the Lighthouse Society’s episode 309 page giving 14 months; counting from the end of June 2020 to mid-August 2021 gives about 13.5 months, so each figure is a rounding of the same stay.The Coast Guard cable failed on April 1, 2021According to Latitude 38, the cable supplying power to the island broke on April 1, 2021, while the Light Hearted page places the failure in early April. The Light Hearted page also mentions that the cable is 30 years old, 2000 feet long and is installed and owned by the Coast Guard. Latitude 38 further states that the Coast Guard installed the current cable in 1991, after a lightning strike irreversibly damaged the previous cable, which dated from the 1960s.The backup battery and generator could power the light but little else. Heveroh told SFGate that the light’s batteries charged whenever she ran the generator, which she described in her KTVU interview as dating from the 1930s and Tom Butt, the mayor of Richmond and president of the nonprofit, said the batteries alone could run the light for only 72 hours.Fundraising, a temporary splice and her move to the SS Red Oak Latitude 38 reported that she launched a GoFundMe campaign after the cable break, which KTVU reported had raised more than $80,000. Latitude 38 cited $150,000 as required to fix the cable only and at least $800,000 for putting it in place. An electrical contractor was later able to splice the remaining broken cable, which KTVU described as a temporary fix and Heveroh explained to Latitude 38 that there were two months during which the island had been without power. The same news outlet stated that the 1962 pier and gangway require fixing as well. CC Pulse reports that she moved off the island in mid-August and became shipkeeper of the SS Red Oak Victory museum in the Richmond shipyards, a role the Lighthouse Society’s episode 309 page also lists.You use AI every day.
